correctness.rationale: From stationary generator obtain phi(k)=prod_{j>=0}(1+q^{2j}k²/alpha²)^-1, alpha=sqrt(r/D). Arbitrarily many factors yield rapid polynomial Fourier decay and C-infinity density. Differentiating D f-rf+(r/q)f(x/q)=0 at x=0 gives f^(2n+2)(0)=-alpha² q^-(2n+1)(1-q^(2n+1))f^(2n)(0), yielding exact alternating derivatives proportional to q^-n² times positive odd q-product. This dominates every finite factorial Gevrey order; normal convergence of residue exponential series gives analyticity off origin. Splitting log phi at N=floor(log(k/alpha)/log(1/q)) yields -t²/a-t-P({t/a})+R with 0<R<=q²e^-2t/(1-q²). Fourier transforming translated logistic sech² gives coefficient -1/[ell sinh(pi²ell/a)] for each ell>=1, so P is nonconstant. Fresh 65-digit checks verified remainder/phase coefficients and derivative identities; all-order proof is analytic.
